pNone_chapter_1: A hazy morning mist blankets a street corner in South Calcutta near Gol Park, softening the outlines of a small tea shop where golden light spills onto the pavement. An elderly man sits on the ground at the edge of the street, cradling a small earthenware tea mug and a few biscuits while the city begins to wake around him. In the background, a few figures in traditional attire gather near the shop’s counter, their forms partially obscured by the thick, cool vapor of the dawn. The atmosphere is quiet and still, illuminated by the pale, diffused glow of a sun that has yet to fully rise.
